::: {.why}
The minimum price increment sets the size of the queue, the size of the queue sets the value of passivity, and the fee schedule decides who wants to be passive at all.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Say what happens to the depth at the touch when the tick is large relative to the spread, and why.
- Compute the round-trip cost of a maker-taker versus a taker-maker fill for 1,000 shares, in dollars, from a real fee schedule.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Read the finmarkets slides on tick size and trading costs. Then, from a real exchange fee schedule, write down the maker rebate and taker fee per hundred shares.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Arithmetic you will use all year: for 1,000 shares of a 50-dollar stock quoted with a 1-cent spread, compute the cost of crossing the spread, then add the taker fee, then compute the same trade done passively with the rebate. Express both as basis points of notional. The ratio between them is the reason execution is a discipline.
